haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rolling deploy halts and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: A background timer re-reads every 5 minutes and swaps in a new non-empty version atomically. A failed or empty read keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries next tick.
haiku-low.q4: Only in process memory, in SecretCache. Key values never go to disk, environment variables, or logs; logs show only names and version ids.
haiku-low.q5: Security on-call is the only role that writes prod secrets or works in provider consoles. The orders-api-prod identity reads them; engineers have no prod read access.
haiku-low.q6: The old keys are in git history and running images, so they are treated as leaked. They become harmless because each is replaced at the provider and the old key is revoked only after confirmation.
haiku-low.q7: Clients do not copy the key at construction. On every outbound call they ask SecretCache for the current key and build the Authorization header.
haiku-low.q8: Platform checks that every pod runs the new image, the pod count matches, and each pod's version endpoint reports the B3 version ids. Other consumers must be moved and the old key shows no recent use.
haiku-low.q9: Store access is set first (B2), then new keys are created and copied into the store (B3). The app switch and YAML key removal ship together in one PR (B4-B7). Old keys are revoked last, after confirmation (B8-B9).
haiku-low.q10: make run sets APP_ENV=local and reads orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own identity. Those hold sandbox or test keys, or local fake clients are used where no sandbox exists.
haiku-low.q11: All three secrets must load and be non-empty, or startup fails and the pod never becomes ready. How a single missing secret is retried is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED as decided. The plan sets no rotation cadence and adds no rotation job; security must answer yes or no and, if yes, an interval.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded at process start, before the server reports ready. /healthz returns 503 until all three are loaded, then 200.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs the secret name and error class and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, so the rolling deploy halts and the old pods keep serving traffic.
sonnet.q3: A timer re-reads the latest version of each secret every 5 minutes. If the value is non-empty and the version id is new, it atomically swaps the cached entry. If the read fails or is empty, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (secret name and error class), and tries again next tick. One secret failing does not block the others.
sonnet.q4: They are held in process memory only, in SecretCache. They must never go to disk, environment variables or logs. Only secret names and version ids are logged.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity has read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. Engineers have no access to prod paths. Write: security on-call only.
sonnet.q6: The old keys have been in git history for two years, so they are treated as leaked. Deleting them from the current file does not remove them from history. They become harmless by being replaced with new keys at the providers and then revoked, after every instance is confirmed to use the new keys. Images built before the change also hold the old keys, so they are blocked or removed (B10).
sonnet.q7: Clients do not copy the key at construction. On each outbound call the client asks SecretCache for the current key and builds the Authorization header. A request already in flight finishes with the key it started with.
sonnet.q8: In the B8 gate, platform checks that every pod runs the new image and the pod list matches the current pod count. Each pod's internal version endpoint must report exactly the B3 version ids for all three keys. Any other consumer found in B1 must have been moved. Where the provider shows last-used, there must be no recent use of the old key. Results are recorded in the ticket, and security on-call approves before revoking.
sonnet.q9: 1) Check providers and find consumers (B1). 2) Create store paths, KMS keys and policies (B2). 3) Create new keys at the providers, keeping the old active, and put them into the store, then validate them with the one-off job (B3). 4) Code change, which switches the app to the store and removes the keys from app.yaml in one PR. It is developed in parallel but must not deploy before B3 passes (B4). 5) Merge and build, then deploy first pod, then the rest (B5 to B7). 6) Confirm all instances (B8), then revoke the old keys at the providers (B9), then block old images (B10). The new keys are created at the providers in B3, and the old ones are revoked last.
sonnet.q10: From the dev secret store at orders-api/dev/*, which holds sandbox or test keys. make run sets APP_ENV=local and the same SecretStore code reads them with the developer's own identity. Providers with no sandbox use a local fake client.
sonnet.q11: All three must load and be non-empty. If one is missing or empty, startup fails. The document does not say explicitly, but this means the app retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready.
sonnet.q12: No schedule is set. Whether to rotate on a schedule is an open question owned by security, and this plan adds no cadence or rotation job. B11 gives a procedure for rotating when needed.
